extra.about: Samuel Riley was born on October 14, 1810, in Meade Township, Belmont County, Ohio. He married Elizabeth Myers in Belmont County on August 18, 1831. A few years later, Samuel's brother Israel Day Riley would marry Elizabeth's younger sister Macy. Samuel and Elizabeth Myers' children were Mary J., Margaret, Elisabeth P., Macy, Richard S., and William. They also helped to raise Elizabeth's sister Rachel's sons, Dixon and John Hays. Samuel and Elizabeth farmed in Belmont and Monroe Counties. Biographical paragraph in the Mead Township section of the book, The History of Belmont and Jefferson Counties, Ohio, published in 1880: 'Samuel Riley was born in Belmont county, Ohio, October 14, 1810. After receiving a limited education, he learned the carpenter trade with his father, and has followed that in connection with farming. In 1830 he went with Samuel Day [his mother's younger brother] on a trading expedition down the river to New Orleans, by which he made $150. With this money he purchased a tract of land in section 7, Mead township, on which he began improvements. August 18, 1831, he married Miss Elizabeth Myers, who was born March 4, 1809. Their union resulted in eight children, three sons and five daughters; five are living. In 1833 he and his wife united with the old Wegee M. E. Church, being among the first members when the class was organized, and have been consistent workers since that time. He has filled the office of township clerk, assessor, trustee and constable. He is still living on the farm where he settled when he was married.'
